docs.title: Home
docs.text:
ComposeFlux

A lightweight GitOps continuous deployment tool for Docker Compose.

GitHub Repository

ComposeFlux automates Docker Compose deployments using GitOps principles. It watches a Git repository, detects changes, and deploys the affected stacks without manual intervention.

ComposeFlux is in beta

Expect heavy refactoring and breaking changes as the project evolves toward v1.0. Progress is tracked in open v1.x.x issues.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description GitOps driven Deployments follow the Git repository Change detection Only stacks affected by a commit are redeployed Lightweight and headless Single container, no UI, no database, no control plane Pure Go implementation Native Docker Compose SDK, no shell execution Offline secrets *.age files in the repository are decrypted in memory Remote secrets Optional Bitwarden Secrets Manager and Infisical support Automatic image updates Scheduled registry checks redeploy stacks when newer images are available Flexible configuration Deployment order and shared environment variables

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Go 1.27+
  • Docker
  • Task

Platform Requirements:

  • Linux: musl-gcc
  • macOS: Xcode Command Line Tools

CGO must be enabled (CGO_ENABLED=1, already set in Taskfile.yml) because ComposeFlux uses the Bitwarden Go SDK, which calls into the Bitwarden Rust SDK via FFI using cgo. See Bitwarden SDK Go instructions.

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/veerendra2/composeflux.git
cd composeflux
go mod download
task install    # Install dev tools
task build
./dist/composeflux --help

docs.title: MkDocs Local Setup
docs.text:
The repository .envrc configures a Python virtual environment for direnv and pyenv users. Without direnv, create the virtual environment manually:

python3 -m venv venv/
source venv/bin/activate

Install MkDocs dependencies:

pip install mkdocs-material

Serve documentation locally:

task docs    # or task serve-docs

docs.title: Available Tasks
docs.text:
task: Available tasks for this project:
* all:                Run comprehensive checks;  format, lint, security and test
* build:              Build the application binary for the current platform
* build-docker:       Build Docker image
* compose:            Run the application in development mode using Docker Compose
* fmt:                Formats all Go source files
* install:            Install required tools and dependencies
* lint:               Run static analysis and code linting using golangci-lint
* run:                Runs the main application
* security:           Run security vulnerability scan
* serve-docs:         Serve MkDocs documentation locally with live reload      (aliases: docs)
* test:               Runs all tests in the project                            (aliases: tests)
* vet:                Examines Go source code and reports suspicious constructs

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Install ComposeFlux on a Docker host and connect it to a Git repository of Compose stacks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A Linux host with Docker Engine and access to the daemon socket at /var/run/docker.sock.
  • The Docker Compose plugin on the host that starts ComposeFlux, for the docker compose commands in this guide. ComposeFlux itself does not require the plugin at runtime.
  • A Git repository reachable over SSH that contains the Compose stacks.
  • Read access to the repository through an SSH key. The key can be mounted into the container or stored in a supported secrets manager.
  • Optional: an Age passphrase or Bitwarden/Infisical credentials for secrets.

See GitHub Deploy Keys for creating a read-only key.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
The following configuration deploys every stack under stacks/ in the repository.

  1. Create a .env file:

    GIT_REPO_URL=git@github.com:user/stacks-repo.git
STACK_PATH=stacks

  2. Create compose.yml:

    services:
  composeflux:
    image: ghcr.io/veerendra2/composeflux:latest
    container_name: composeflux
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      GIT_REPO_URL: ${GIT_REPO_URL}
      STACK_PATH: ${STACK_PATH}
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy:/.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa:ro
      - compose-stack:/opt/compose-stack

volumes:
  compose-stack:

  3. Start ComposeFlux:

    docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f

The mounted key must be readable by the container and must not have a passphrase. The named volume keeps the Git clone between restarts. If the initial sync fails, the process exits with the error in the log.

The SSH deploy key can also be fetched from a remote secrets manager (Bitwarden or Infisical) by setting GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF. For Bitwarden the value is the secret ID; for Infisical it is the secret key name. See GitHub Deploy Keys.

Note

When GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF is set, remove the read-only key mount from the Compose file. ComposeFlux writes the fetched key to GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH, and a read-only mount makes that write fail at startup.

docs.title: Deploy with Ansible
docs.text:
The ansible-role-composeflux-deploy role installs the same deployment on a target host.

ansible-galaxy role install veerendra2.composeflux_deploy
ansible-galaxy collection install community.docker   # required by the role

- hosts: servers
  become: true
  roles:
    - role: veerendra2.composeflux_deploy
      vars:
        composeflux_git_repo_url: "git@github.com:user/infra-repo.git"
        composeflux_stack_path: "servers/myhost"

        # Provide either a local key or a secrets manager reference.
        composeflux_ssh_key_local_path: "~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy"
        # composeflux_ssh_key_secret_ref: "SSH_PRIVATE_KEY"

        # Optional secrets.
        composeflux_age_passphrase: "{{ vault_age_passphrase }}"
        # composeflux_infisical_client_id: "{{ vault_infisical_client_id }}"
        # composeflux_infisical_client_secret: "{{ vault_infisical_client_secret }}"
        # composeflux_infisical_environment: "prod"
        # composeflux_infisical_project_id: "project-id"

ansible-playbook playbook.yml
ansible-playbook playbook.yml --tags sync   # force a reconciliation now

Role variables map to the environment variables below. See the role defaults for the full list.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Every option has an environment variable and a command-line flag. Flags apply to both run and sync.

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description GIT_REPO_URL --repo-url required SSH URL of the Git repository. STACK_PATH --stack-path required Directory in the repository that contains the stacks. CONFIG_FILE --config-file stack.yml Path of the shared stack configuration file, relative to STACK_PATH. GIT_INTERVAL --git-interval 5m Git polling interval. Must be greater than zero. HEALTH_RECONCILE_INTERVAL --health-interval 0 Health reconciliation interval. 0 disables it. IMAGE_UPDATE_SCHEDULE --image-update-schedule empty Cron expression for image update checks. Empty disables it. PRUNE_INTERVAL --prune-interval 24h Docker resource prune interval. 0 disables it. See Resource pruning before enabling it on a shared host.

docs.title: Git
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description GIT_BRANCH --branch main Branch to track. GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH --ssh-key-path /.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa SSH private key path inside the container. GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF --deploy-key-secret-ref empty Secret name or ID in the configured secrets manager. Requires Bitwarden or Infisical. GIT_CLONE_PATH --clone-path /opt/compose-stack Local clone directory.

docs.title: Offline secrets
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description AGE_PASSPHRASE --age-passphrase empty Passphrase for *.age files. Empty disables offline secrets.

docs.title: Bitwarden
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description BITWARDEN_ACCESS_TOKEN --bitwarden-access-token required with Bitwarden Machine account access token. BITWARDEN_ORGANIZATION_ID --bitwarden-organization-id required with Bitwarden Organization ID. BITWARDEN_PROJECT_ID --bitwarden-project-id required with Bitwarden Project ID. BITWARDEN_API_URL --bitwarden-api-url https://vault.bitwarden.com/api API URL. BITWARDEN_IDENTITY_URL --bitwarden-identity-url https://vault.bitwarden.com/identity Identity URL.

docs.title: Infisical
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID --infisical-client-id required with Infisical Universal Auth client ID. INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET --infisical-client-secret required with Infisical Universal Auth client secret. INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT --infisical-environment required with Infisical Environment slug, for example prod. INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID --infisical-project-id required with Infisical Project ID. INFISICAL_SECRET_PATH --infisical-secret-path / Secret path. Comma-separated paths are allowed; later paths override earlier ones. INFISICAL_SITE_URL --infisical-site-url https://app.infisical.com Site URL.

docs.title: Docker and logging
docs.text: Environment variable Flag Default Description REMOVE_ORPHANS --remove-orphans true Remove containers that are not defined in the Compose project. LOG_LEVEL --log-level INFO DEBUG, INFO, WARN, or ERROR. Values are case-insensitive. LOG_FORMAT --log-format console console or json. LOG_ADD_SOURCE --log-add-source false Include the source file and line in log records.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Description composeflux run Daemon mode. Polls Git and reconciles continuously. This is the default. composeflux sync Performs one forced reconciliation, then exits.

To run a one-shot sync against a running container:

docker exec composeflux /composeflux sync

ComposeFlux validates the configuration before starting. GIT_INTERVAL must be greater than zero, health and prune intervals must not be negative, and a non-empty IMAGE_UPDATE_SCHEDULE must be a valid cron expression. Invalid values stop startup.

docs.title: Full Compose example
docs.text:
The example below lists every option. Uncomment only the options in use.

services:
  composeflux:
    image: ghcr.io/veerendra2/composeflux:latest
    container_name: composeflux
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      # Required
      GIT_REPO_URL: ${GIT_REPO_URL}
      STACK_PATH: ${STACK_PATH}

      # Git
      # GIT_BRANCH: main
      # GIT_INTERVAL: 5m
      # GIT_CLONE_PATH: /opt/compose-stack
      # GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH: /.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa
      # GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF: ""

      # Stack configuration
      # CONFIG_FILE: stack.yml

      # Offline secrets
      # AGE_PASSPHRASE: ${AGE_PASSPHRASE}

      # Bitwarden Secrets Manager
      # BITWARDEN_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${BITWARDEN_ACCESS_TOKEN}
      # BITWARDEN_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${BITWARDEN_ORGANIZATION_ID}
      # BITWARDEN_PROJECT_ID: ${BITWARDEN_PROJECT_ID}
      # BITWARDEN_API_URL: https://vault.bitwarden.com/api
      # BITWARDEN_IDENTITY_URL: https://vault.bitwarden.com/identity

      # Infisical Secrets Manager
      # INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID: ${INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID}
      # INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET: ${INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET}
      # INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT: prod
      # INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID: ${INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID}
      # INFISICAL_SECRET_PATH: /
      # INFISICAL_SITE_URL: https://app.infisical.com

      # Reconciliation and pruning
      # HEALTH_RECONCILE_INTERVAL: 5m
      # IMAGE_UPDATE_SCHEDULE: "0 3 * * *"
      # PRUNE_INTERVAL: 24h

      # Docker
      # REMOVE_ORPHANS: "true"

      # Logging
      # LOG_LEVEL: INFO
      # LOG_FORMAT: console
      # LOG_ADD_SOURCE: "false"

    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      # Local key only. Omit when GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF is set.
      - ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy:/.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa:ro
      - compose-stack:/opt/compose-stack

volumes:
  compose-stack:

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
# Follow logs. The initial sync reports deployed stacks and any failures.
docker compose logs -f

# List managed containers.
docker ps --filter "label=composeflux.managed=true"

# List Compose projects known to Docker.
docker compose ls

A successful sync logs a Stack deployment summary with counts for deployed, failed, and skipped stacks.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: ComposeFlux is a GitOps continuous deployment tool for Docker Compose. It reconciles Docker stacks on a host from a Git repository.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: ComposeFlux reconciles the Docker stacks located under a path (STACK_PATH) in a Git repository, authenticating with a deploy key. It is standalone: there is no central management service, UI, or database. Managing stacks on a host therefore means running ComposeFlux on that host and pointing STACK_PATH at the directory that holds those stacks.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text: Stacks are organized into directories under STACK_PATH, ideally one directory per server.

docs.title: Stack Path
docs.text:
STACK_PATH defines where ComposeFlux looks for stacks. The stacks must be flat: ComposeFlux scans that directory for drift and reconciles the stacks found in it.

The image below shows multiple standalone ComposeFlux instances running on different servers, all pointing at the same Git repository with different STACK_PATH values.

docs.title: Stacks
docs.text:
A stack is a Docker Compose directory that contains a Compose file and its related configuration, including an optional Age vault.

stacks/                     STACK_PATH
├── stack.yml               optional shared configuration
├── shared.env.age          optional secrets for every stack
├── traefik/
│   ├── compose.yml
│   └── traefik.env.age     optional secrets for this stack
├── nextcloud/
│   └── compose.yml
└── jellyfin/
    └── docker-compose.yml

During reconciliation, ComposeFlux lists the directories in STACK_PATH and looks for compose.yaml, compose.yml, docker-compose.yml, or docker-compose.yaml, plus a matching override file. Directories without a Compose file are ignored. Discovery is one level deep: nested directories are not scanned on their own. A stack can still be modularized or include another Compose file, provided the referenced files are inside the same repository, where changes to them trigger reconciliation. Remote includes (Git or OCI) are passed to Compose when the project is loaded, so they can affect the deployed project, but ComposeFlux does not track them: a change to a remote include does not trigger a deployment, and secrets in the remote location are not loaded. Paths that escape the repository are rejected.

The project name must match the directory name

Do not set a name: in the Compose file that differs from the stack directory name. ComposeFlux treats the directory name as the Compose project name and rejects a project whose resolved name differs.

docs.title: Stack configuration
docs.text:
An optional stack.yml in STACK_PATH controls deployment order and defines environment variables shared by all stacks. The file name is configurable with CONFIG_FILE and is resolved relative to STACK_PATH.

startup_order:
  - traefik

envs:
  DOMAIN: homeserver.local
  TZ: America/New_York
  ENVIRONMENT: production
  • startup_order lists stacks that must deploy first. The remaining stacks deploy afterwards in no guaranteed order.
  • envs are available for Compose interpolation in every stack.
  • Names in startup_order must match directory names. Unknown names are reported in the log and skipped.
  • A missing stack.yml is allowed. A malformed or unreadable file stops the current reconciliation pass.

docs.title: Health reconciliation
docs.text:
Set HEALTH_RECONCILE_INTERVAL to enable periodic health checks; they are disabled by default. When enabled, ComposeFlux redeploys any managed stack that contains an unhealthy container. Git is not pulled for this recovery.

A container is healthy when either of these is true:

  • The container is running and its health status is not unhealthy.
  • The container has exited with code 0 and carries the composeflux.init: "true" label, which marks a one-shot or init container as an expected exit.

Every other state is unhealthy, including restarting, paused, dead, and exited without the init label. A stack is unhealthy when any of its containers is unhealthy. After three consecutive failed deployments, ComposeFlux stops trying the stack until the next successful Git sync or image update.

docs.title: Automatic image updates
docs.text:
Set IMAGE_UPDATE_SCHEDULE to a cron expression to check for new images. ComposeFlux compares the local and remote image digests for each stack. When a newer digest is available, it pulls the images and redeploys the stack. Images built locally or pinned by digest are skipped, and an image that is missing locally is treated as needing an update.

Add composeflux.image-update.exclude: "true" to any service to exclude the stack. If a scheduled check is still running, the next invocation is skipped.

docs.title: Resource pruning
docs.text:
PRUNE_INTERVAL defaults to 24h. Set it to 0 to disable pruning.

Pruning applies to the whole Docker host

Pruning is not limited to ComposeFlux stacks. It removes all unused volumes, all dangling images, and all build cache. Containers and networks are not pruned.

Pruning runs only when every stack under STACK_PATH is running in Docker, healthy, and not suspended. Otherwise the cycle is skipped and a warning is logged.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
ComposeFlux supports two secret sources, which can be used together:

  • Offline secrets: age-encrypted dotenv files (*.age) stored in the Git repository and decrypted in memory.
  • Remote secrets: Bitwarden Secrets Manager or Infisical. Only one remote provider can be configured.

docs.title: Offline Secrets
docs.text:
Note

Only age with passphrase encryption is supported. Files with the .age extension are discovered automatically and decrypted with AGE_PASSPHRASE (--age-passphrase).

Offline secrets are dotenv files encrypted with a passphrase and committed to the stack repository. During reconciliation ComposeFlux discovers the *.age files that apply to a stack, decrypts each one in memory, parses it as dotenv, and exports the keys as environment variables for Compose interpolation while the stack is brought up. Plaintext is never written to disk, and the keys are available to the Compose file for interpolation only.

A .age file inside a stack directory provides secrets for that stack. A .age file in the root of STACK_PATH provides secrets for every stack in that stack path, that is, shared secrets.

Create a dotenv file containing the values to encrypt:

TOKEN=my-token

Encrypt it with a passphrase and remove the plaintext file:

age -p -o .env.secrets.age .env_secrets
rm .env_secrets

The encrypted file is kept next to the stack it belongs to:

servers/wg1-ams/wg-easy/
├── .env.secrets.age
├── compose.override.yml
└── compose.yml

The Compose file references the exported keys:

name: wg-easy

services:
  wg-easy:
    image: ghcr.io/wg-easy/wg-easy:latest
    environment:
      TOKEN: ${TOKEN} # decrypted from the .age vault and exported while bringing up the stack

See Offline Secrets with Age for the full workflow.

docs.title: Remote secrets
docs.text:
Note

Only Bitwarden Secrets Manager and Infisical are supported as remote providers.

One remote provider can be configured at a time. Values are fetched whenever ComposeFlux reconciles a stack. After changing a secret in the provider, run composeflux sync to apply it.

ComposeFlux does not inject every secret into every container. A value reaches a container only when the Compose service references it:

services:
  app:
    image: myapp:latest
    environment:
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}
  • Bitwarden Secrets Manager (How-to Guide)
  • Infisical Secrets Manager (How-to Guide)

docs.title: Git checkout ownership
docs.text:
Warning

Git is the source of truth for the checkout at GIT_CLONE_PATH. Before the startup checkout and before each sync, ComposeFlux discards local changes to tracked files and logs the affected paths. This includes changes written by containers through bind mounts. Untracked files are preserved, but a file required by the target revision can be replaced. Mutable application data must stay outside tracked files.

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
ComposeFlux adds composeflux.managed, composeflux.version, and composeflux.deployed-at labels to every service during deployment. The managed label can be used to list stacks:

docker ps --filter "label=composeflux.managed=true"

Besides the labels added by ComposeFlux, services can carry labels that control reconciliation.

docs.title: Suspend
docs.text:
composeflux.health.suspend

When this label is set on any service in the Compose file, ComposeFlux stops managing the stack: no Git deployment, health recovery, or image updates, and the resource prune cycle is skipped.

Example

---
name: actualbudget
services:
  actualbudget:
    image: docker.io/actualbudget/actual-server:latest
    container_name: actualbudget
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - composeflux.health.suspend=true
    hostname: actualbudget

docs.title: Init
docs.text:
composeflux.init

When health reconciliation is enabled, a one-shot container in a stack can be marked so that ComposeFlux does not treat its exit as a failure. Add this label to the service.

Example

---
name: valkey
services:
  init-change-ownership: # one-shot container
    image: busybox:latest
    labels:
      - composeflux.init=true # health checks succeed even though this container exits with code 0
    volumes:
      - valkey_data:/tmp/change-ownership
    environment:
      PUID: ${PUID}
      PGID: ${PGID}
    command: chown -R ${PUID}:${PGID} /tmp/change-ownership

  valkey:
    image: valkey/valkey:8-alpine
    container_name: valkey
    depends_on:
      init-change-ownership:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    volumes:
      - valkey_data:/data
    user: ${PUID}:${PGID}
    hostname: valkey
volumes:
  valkey_data:
    name: valkey_data

docs.title: Exclude Image Update
docs.text:
composeflux.image-update.exclude

This label excludes a stack from automatic image updates.

Example

---
name: actualbudget
services:
  actualbudget:
    image: docker.io/actualbudget/actual-server:latest
    container_name: actualbudget
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - composeflux.image-update.exclude=true
    hostname: actualbudget

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Stack discovery is one level deep.
  • No central controller or multi-server orchestration.
  • No rolling updates or zero-downtime deployments.
  • No built-in monitoring or alerting.

docs.title: Offline Secrets with Age
docs.text: ComposeFlux can decrypt age encrypted files stored in the Git repository and use their values for Compose interpolation. Decryption happens in memory; plaintext is not written to disk.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• ComposeFlux reads *.age files directly from the stack root, each stack directory, and directories pulled in through include or extends. Subdirectories are not scanned recursively.
  • Each file must be a dotenv file encrypted with a passphrase (age -p). ASCII-armored and binary files are both supported.
  • Values are merged in this order: stack root, stack directory, included directory. A later value overrides an earlier one. Files in the same directory are merged in filename order.
  • Offline secrets also override remote secrets. A stack-directory value takes precedence over a stack-root value, which takes precedence over a value fetched from Bitwarden or Infisical.
  • A *.age file must be a regular file. Symbolic links are rejected.
  • Values are available only for Compose interpolation. A container receives a value only when its service references it, for example DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}.
  • Committing a change to a *.age file triggers a redeploy of the affected stacks.

docs.title: Directory layout
docs.text:
stacks/                     STACK_PATH
├── stack.yml
├── shared.env.age          applies to every stack
├── traefik/
│   ├── compose.yml
│   └── traefik.env.age     applies to traefik only
└── nextcloud/
    ├── compose.yml
    └── secrets.env.age     applies to nextcloud only

docs.title: Encrypt a file
docs.text:
1. Install the age CLI:

    # Debian or Ubuntu
apt install age

# macOS
brew install age

  2. Create a dotenv file with the values to encrypt:

    DATABASE_PASSWORD=supersecretpassword
API_KEY=1234567890abcdef

  3. Encrypt the file with a passphrase. The -a option stores the ciphertext as text:

    age -p -a -o stacks/nextcloud/secrets.env.age secrets.env

  4. Remove the plaintext file:

    rm secrets.env

  5. Commit and push the encrypted file:

    git add stacks/nextcloud/secrets.env.age
git commit -m "Add nextcloud secrets"
git push

docs.title: Configure ComposeFlux
docs.text:
Set AGE_PASSPHRASE (or the --age-passphrase flag) to the passphrase used during encryption. When it is empty, offline secrets are disabled and no *.age files are read.

services:
  composeflux:
    image: ghcr.io/veerendra2/composeflux:latest
    environment:
      GIT_REPO_URL: git@github.com:user/stacks-repo.git
      STACK_PATH: stacks
      AGE_PASSPHRASE: ${AGE_PASSPHRASE}
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy:/.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa:ro
      - compose-stack:/opt/compose-stack

volumes:
  compose-stack:

Keep the passphrase in a protected environment variable or a local .env file. Do not commit it to the Compose file or the stacks repository.

docs.title: Use the values
docs.text:
Reference the keys in a stack's Compose file:

services:
  app:
    image: myapp:latest
    environment:
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}
      API_KEY: ${API_KEY}

Keys that are not referenced are not passed to containers.

docs.title: Edit an encrypted file
docs.text:
The agedit helper decrypts a file into a temporary file, opens it in vim, and re-encrypts it only when the content changed.

mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
curl -fsSL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/veerendra2/35c0b81980e81fcb11a86e6cde2f9508/raw -o ~/.local/bin/agedit
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/agedit

agedit stacks/nextcloud/secrets.env.age

The script requires age and vim. It writes binary age files, which ComposeFlux supports.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause failed to decrypt age file Wrong AGE_PASSPHRASE, or the file was encrypted to an age identity instead of a passphrase. age secret file must not be a symbolic link Replace the link with the encrypted file itself. A file is not loaded The file is nested in a subdirectory, is not located next to a Compose file or stack root, or does not end in .age. A variable is empty in a container The service does not reference the variable in its Compose configuration.

A decryption failure stops the current reconciliation pass. Fix the passphrase or the file, then wait for the next sync or run composeflux sync.

docs.title: Bitwarden Secrets Manager
docs.text: Configure Bitwarden Secrets Manager as a remote secrets provider. ComposeFlux fetches every secret in the configured project and exposes each value under its secret key name.

docs.title: 1. Create a project
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Bitwarden.
  2. Open Secrets Manager.
  3. Click New Project and create a project for ComposeFlux.

docs.title: 2. Add secrets
docs.text:
Add the keys referenced by the stacks, for example DATABASE_URL or API_KEY.

To fetch the Git deploy key from Bitwarden, create a secret that contains the private key and copy its secret ID. See Store the key in a secrets manager.

docs.title: 3. Create a machine account
docs.text:
1. Open the Machine Accounts tab.
  2. Click New Machine Account.
  3. Assign the project created above.
  4. Set the permission to Can read.
  5. Click Save.

docs.title: 4. Create an access token
docs.text:
1. Open the machine account.
  2. Open the Access tokens tab.
  3. Click Create access token.
  4. Copy the token and store it securely.

docs.title: 5. Configure ComposeFlux
docs.text:
Set the following values. The organization ID, project ID, API URL, and identity URL are shown in the machine account configuration.

BITWARDEN_ACCESS_TOKEN=<access-token>
BITWARDEN_ORGANIZATION_ID=<organization-id>
BITWARDEN_PROJECT_ID=<project-id>

# Optional: only when fetching the SSH deploy key from Bitwarden
GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF=<secret-id>

# Optional: only for self-hosted Bitwarden
# BITWARDEN_API_URL=https://vault.bitwarden.com/api
# BITWARDEN_IDENTITY_URL=https://vault.bitwarden.com/identity

docs.title: Use the values
docs.text:
Reference the keys in a stack's Compose file:

services:
  app:
    image: myapp:latest
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL}
      API_KEY: ${API_KEY}

Keys that are not referenced are not passed to containers. After changing a secret in Bitwarden, run composeflux sync to apply it.

docs.title: GitHub Deploy Keys
docs.text: A deploy key gives ComposeFlux read-only SSH access to the stacks repository. The same approach works with other Git providers.

docs.title: Generate a key pair
docs.text:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "composeflux-deploy-key" -f ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy

This creates the private key ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy and the public key ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy.pub. Do not set a passphrase; ComposeFlux runs unattended.

docs.title: Add the public key to GitHub
docs.text:
1. Copy the public key:

    cat ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy.pub

  2. Open the repository on GitHub.

  3. Go to Settings, then Deploy keys, and click Add deploy key.
  4. Paste the key and leave write access disabled.

docs.title: Provide the private key to ComposeFlux
docs.text: Use one of the following options.

docs.title: Mount the key
docs.text:
Mount the private key at GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH. The default path is /.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa.

services:
  composeflux:
    image: ghcr.io/veerendra2/composeflux:latest
    environment:
      GIT_REPO_URL: git@github.com:user/repo.git
      STACK_PATH: stacks
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy:/.ssh/composeflux_id_rsa:ro
      - compose-stack:/opt/compose-stack

volumes:
  compose-stack:

docs.title: Store the key in a secrets manager
docs.text:
This option requires Bitwarden or Infisical credentials. Set GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF to the secret reference:

  • Bitwarden: the secret ID.
  • Infisical: the secret key name, for example SSH_PRIVATE_KEY.

At startup, ComposeFlux fetches the value and writes it to GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH with mode 0600. When the reference is empty, ComposeFlux uses the key already present at that path.

Do not also mount the key at GIT_SSH_KEY_PATH: a read-only mount makes the write fail at startup.

environment:
  GIT_REPO_URL: git@github.com:user/repo.git
  STACK_PATH: stacks
  GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF: SSH_PRIVATE_KEY
  INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID: ${INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID}
  INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET: ${INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET}
  INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT: prod
  INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID: ${INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID}

See Bitwarden or Infisical for adding the secret.

docs.title: Test access
docs.text:
ssh -i ~/.ssh/composeflux_deploy -T git@github.com

A successful test prints a message that the key authenticated but does not provide shell access.

docs.title: Infisical Secrets Manager
docs.text: Configure Infisical as a remote secrets provider. ComposeFlux fetches secrets from the configured project, environment, and paths, and exposes each value under its secret key name.

docs.title: 1. Create a project
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Infisical.
  2. Open the Overview tab.
  3. Click Add New Project and create a project for ComposeFlux.

docs.title: 2. Choose an environment
docs.text:
ComposeFlux uses INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT, so an environment slug is required.

  1. Open the project.
  2. Create or select an environment, for example prod.
  3. Note the environment slug.

docs.title: 3. Add secrets
docs.text:
Add the keys referenced by the stacks, for example DATABASE_PASSWORD or API_KEY.

To fetch the Git deploy key from Infisical, create a secret named SSH_PRIVATE_KEY and copy the private key content. See Store the key in a secrets manager.

docs.title: 4. Optional: organize secrets in folders
docs.text:
Set INFISICAL_SECRET_PATH to the folder used by ComposeFlux. The default is /.

Use a comma-separated list to read secrets from several folders, for example /generic,/apps/prod:

  • If a path cannot be read, ComposeFlux logs a warning and continues with the other paths.
  • If every path fails, the fetch fails.
  • If the same key exists in several paths, the last path's value takes precedence.

A common layout is shared secrets in /generic and environment overrides in /apps/prod.

docs.title: 5. Create a machine identity
docs.text:
1. Open Project Settings, then Access Control, then Machine Identities.
  2. Click Add Machine Identity to Project.
  3. Enter a name and set the role to Viewer.

docs.title: 6. Create client credentials
docs.text:
1. Open the machine identity.
  2. In the Authentication tab, expand Universal Auth.
  3. Click Add Client Secrets.
  4. Copy the client ID and client secret.

docs.title: 7. Configure ComposeFlux
docs.text:
INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID=<client-id>
INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET=<client-secret>
INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT=prod
INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID=<project-id>

# Optional
# INFISICAL_SECRET_PATH=/
# INFISICAL_SITE_URL=https://app.infisical.com
# GIT_DEPLOY_KEY_SECRET_REF=SSH_PRIVATE_KEY

The project ID is shown in the project settings.

docs.title: Use the values
docs.text:
Reference the keys in a stack's Compose file:

services:
  app:
    image: myapp:latest
    environment:
      DATABASE_PASSWORD: ${DATABASE_PASSWORD}
      API_KEY: ${API_KEY}

Keys that are not referenced are not passed to containers. After changing a secret in Infisical, run composeflux sync to apply it.
